6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: When a square is rotated completely around its centre (360 degrees), how many times does it look exactly the same as its original position?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A square has a rotational symmetry of order 4. This means it looks the same 4 times during a full 360-degree rotation (at 90, 180, 270, and 360 degrees).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry can a circle have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A circle has an infinite number of lines of symmetry, as any line passing through its center will divide it into two identical halves.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these capital letters has both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'H' has both a horizontal line of symmetry (folding it across its middle) and a vertical line of symmetry (folding it top to bottom).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these shapes exhibits rotational symmetry (looks the same after turning less than a full circle)?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rectangle has rotational symmetry of order 2, meaning it looks the same after a 180-degree turn. The other shapes generally do not have rotational symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A certain letter of the English alphabet has exactly one line of symmetry, which is horizontal. Which letter could it be?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'B' has exactly one line of symmetry, and this line is horizontal. Letters A, M have vertical symmetry, and Z has no line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A line that divides a figure into two identical halves, such that one half is a mirror image of the other, is called a:
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The definition of a line of symmetry is a line that divides a figure into two parts that are exact mirror images of each other.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following letters of the English alphabet has no line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Letters 'A', 'O', and 'M' each have at least one line of symmetry, while the letter 'S' does not have any line that divides it into identical mirror halves.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A rectangle has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rectangle has two lines of symmetry; these lines join the midpoints of its opposite sides.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: An equilateral triangle has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three lines of symmetry, with each line passing through a vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these shapes has an infinite number of lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Any line passing through the center of a circle will divide it into two identical halves, and there are infinitely many such lines.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following objects typically exhibits line symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A butterfly is a classic example of an object with bilateral (line) symmetry, where one half is a mirror image of the other.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which letter among the following has a horizontal line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'B' can be folded horizontally along its center to create two identical mirror halves. 'A', 'M', and 'T' have vertical lines of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which letter among the following has a vertical line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'H' can be folded vertically along its center to form two identical halves. 'E' and 'C' have horizontal lines of symmetry, while 'K' generally has none.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which letter has both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'X' can be folded both horizontally and vertically to produce two identical mirror halves, indicating it has both types of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following shapes is generally asymmetrical?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A scalene triangle has all sides of different lengths and all angles of different measures, which means it has no line of symmetry and is therefore asymmetrical.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A standard door has how many lines of symmetry (ignoring hinges and handle)?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A standard rectangular door has one vertical line of symmetry, running down its center.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: If you place a mirror along the line of symmetry of a figure, what would you see?
options: The other half of the figure
Only one half of the figure
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The line of symmetry acts as a mirror line, and one half of the figure is the exact mirror image of the other half.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: If half of a figure is given and a line of symmetry is drawn, to complete the figure, you need to draw its:
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: To complete a symmetrical figure, you need to draw the mirror image (reflection) of the given half across the line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: All regular polygons have:
options: As many lines of symmetry as sides
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A regular polygon has a line of symmetry for each of its sides. For example, a regular pentagon has 5 lines of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rhombus has two lines of symmetry, which are its diagonals.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A kite has exactly one line of symmetry, which is its main diagonal connecting the two non-equal angles.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A parallelogram, which is not a rhombus or a rectangle, has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A general parallelogram (one that is not a special case like a rhombus or rectangle) has no line of symmetry, though it does have point symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: An isosceles trapezium has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: An isosceles trapezium has one line of symmetry, which passes through the midpoints of its parallel sides.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following letters has no line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Letters H, O, and T all possess lines of symmetry (H and O have both horizontal and vertical, T has vertical). The letter 'N' does not have any line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following digits has a horizontal line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The digit '0' (zero) has both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry. The other digits listed do not have a horizontal line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these figures is generally symmetrical, while others are typically not?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A human face generally exhibits bilateral symmetry. Tree leaves, bricks (unless perfect), and mountains are typically irregular or asymmetrical.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides. A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so it has 5 lines of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A figure is symmetrical if it can be divided into two parts that are ______ of each other.
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Symmetry means that one part of a figure is a perfect mirror image of the other part along a line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Another name for a line of symmetry is:
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The terms 'line of symmetry' and 'axis of symmetry' are often used interchangeably to describe the line that divides a figure into two mirror-image halves.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry does a semicircle have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A semicircle has exactly one line of symmetry, which is perpendicular to its diameter and passes through its center.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: I am a quadrilateral. I have all sides equal in length. I have exactly two lines of symmetry. What shape am I?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A square has all sides equal but has four lines of symmetry. A rhombus has all sides equal and exactly two lines of symmetry (its diagonals).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Symmetrical patterns are often found in:
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Symmetry is a fundamental principle used in art, architecture, and design to create balance, harmony, and visual appeal.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a figure with line symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Heart shapes, balanced seesaws, and spectacles (typically) exhibit line symmetry. A winding river is naturally irregular and does not typically have line symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following best describes a 'line of symmetry'?
options: A line that connects two opposite corners of a shape.
A line that divides a figure into two identical mirror halves.
A line that passes through the center of a figure.
A line that is always horizontal.
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A line of symmetry is a line that divides a figure into two parts such that if the figure is folded along that line, the two parts match exactly, acting as mirror images of each other.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these letters has exactly one line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'A' has one vertical line of symmetry. Letters like H, X, and O have multiple lines of symmetry (H and X have two, O has infinite).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: What is another name for line symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Line symmetry is also known as reflection symmetry because one half of the figure is a mirror image (reflection) of the other half across the line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Does a circle have lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A circle is perfectly symmetrical. Any line passing through its center is a line of symmetry, meaning it has infinitely many lines of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which real-life object often shows clear line symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A butterfly's body plan typically exhibits clear line symmetry, with its left wing being a mirror image of its right wing across its central body axis.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: If you fold a sheet of paper and cut out a shape along the fold, what kind of symmetry will the cut-out shape have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: When a shape is cut along a fold, the fold line itself acts as a line of symmetry, ensuring the resulting shape has line symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these figures is symmetrical?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A kite has exactly one line of symmetry, which passes along its longer diagonal. Scalene triangles and general parallelograms do not have line symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: What is the minimum number of sides a regular polygon must have to exhibit line symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A regular polygon, by definition, has all sides and angles equal. The simplest regular polygon is an equilateral triangle (3 sides), which has 3 lines of symmetry. Any regular polygon with 3 or more sides will have line symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A rectangle (that is not a square) has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rectangle has two lines of symmetry, which pass through the midpoints of opposite sides (one horizontal, one vertical). It does not have diagonal lines of symmetry unless it is also a square.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these letters has both a horizontal and a vertical line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'H' has both a horizontal line of symmetry (dividing it into top and bottom halves) and a vertical line of symmetry (dividing it into left and right halves).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these shapes does *not* have any line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A scalene triangle has all sides of different lengths and all angles of different measures, hence it does not possess any line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: What is the number of lines of symmetry in the letter 'X'?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'X' has two lines of symmetry: one horizontal and one vertical, both passing through its center.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A rhombus (that is not a square) has how many lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rhombus has two lines of symmetry, which are its diagonals. These diagonals divide the rhombus into two congruent mirror images.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: The line segment connecting a point to its reflection image across a line of symmetry is always ______ to the line of symmetry.
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: When a point is reflected across a line of symmetry, the line segment connecting the original point to its image is always perpendicular to the line of symmetry, and the line of symmetry bisects this segment.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles. It has exactly one line of symmetry, which passes through the vertex angle and the midpoint of the opposite base.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of these numbers has a vertical line of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The digit '8' has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry. When a vertical line is drawn through its center, the left half mirrors the right half.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A figure has exactly two lines of symmetry. Which of these shapes could it be?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, a square has 4, and a regular pentagon has 5. A rectangle that is not a square has exactly two lines of symmetry (horizontal and vertical through the midpoints of its sides).

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following statements is true about a mirror image?
options: It is always smaller than the original object.
It is an exact copy but flipped (laterally inverted).
It is always rotated by 90 degrees.
It is only visible in curved mirrors.
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A mirror image is an exact replica of the original object in terms of size and shape, but it is laterally inverted (flipped horizontally), meaning left and right appear reversed.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Consider the letter 'S'. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'S' does not have any line of symmetry. If you try to fold it along any line, the two halves will not match. It does, however, have rotational symmetry of order 2.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A quadrilateral has exactly four lines of symmetry. What type of quadrilateral is it?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Only a square possesses exactly four lines of symmetry: two connecting midpoints of opposite sides and two connecting opposite vertices. A rhombus and rectangle (non-square) have two, and a general parallelogram has none.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: When a symmetrical figure is folded along its line of symmetry, what happens to the two halves?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The definition of a line of symmetry is that it divides a figure into two identical mirror halves that overlap perfectly when the figure is folded along that line.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A figure has 'n' lines of symmetry. If 'n' is an odd number, which of these regular polygons could it be?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: Regular polygons have 'n' lines of symmetry, where 'n' is the number of sides. A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so it has 5 (an odd number) lines of symmetry. A square has 4, a regular hexagon has 6, and a rectangle has 2.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which of the following letters has no line of symmetry but has rotational symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: The letter 'N' has no line of symmetry but exhibits rotational symmetry of order 2 (it looks the same after a 180-degree rotation). M, T, and D all have at least one line of symmetry.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: A figure is symmetric about a line if, for every point P on the figure, there is a corresponding point P' such that the line of symmetry is the ______ of the segment PP'.
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: For a figure to be symmetric about a line, the line of symmetry must be the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting any point on the figure to its reflected image.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Imagine cutting out a heart shape from a folded paper. Which type of symmetry will the heart shape always possess?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: When cutting a heart shape from a folded paper, the fold creates a vertical line of symmetry down the middle of the heart, making the left and right halves mirror images.

6::Mathematics::symmetry.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::symmetry.question: Which pair of figures has the same number of lines of symmetry?
6::Mathematics::symmetry.explanation: A rhombus (non-square) has 2 lines of symmetry (its diagonals). A rectangle (non-square) also has 2 lines of symmetry (through midpoints of opposite sides).

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If a temperature of 5 degrees Celsius *below zero* is represented as -5°C, how would a temperature of 10 degrees Celsius *above zero* be represented?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Numbers below zero are represented by negative integers, and numbers above zero are represented by positive integers. So, 10 degrees Celsius above zero is +10°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following numbers is an integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Integers are whole numbers, including positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero. Fractions and decimals (unless they represent a whole number) are not integers.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: On a number line, which integer is located to the *left* of -3?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On a number line, numbers decrease as you move to the left. Therefore, -4 is to the left of -3 and is smaller than -3.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Arrange the following integers in *ascending* order: 5, -2, 0, -7, 3.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Ascending order means arranging numbers from smallest to largest. Negative numbers are smaller than zero and positive numbers. The further a negative number is from zero, the smaller it is.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the successor of -5?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The successor of a number is the number immediately following it on the number line, obtained by adding 1. So, the successor of -5 is -5 + 1 = -4.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A submarine is at 200 meters below sea level. If '0' represents sea level, how would you represent the submarine's position?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Positions below a reference point (like sea level or zero) are represented by negative numbers. Therefore, 200 meters below sea level is -200 m.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the value of (-8) + 3?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: When adding integers with different signs, find the difference between their absolute values (8 - 3 = 5) and use the sign of the number with the larger absolute value (which is -8, so the result is negative).

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: In a quiz, Team A scored -15, 20, 10 in three rounds, and Team B scored 10, -5, 15. Which team scored more?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Team A's total score = -15 + 20 + 10 = 15. Team B's total score = 10 + (-5) + 15 = 20. Since 20 is greater than 15, Team B scored more.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Every positive integer is greater than every negative integer.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Positive numbers are always greater than negative numbers. Zero is neither positive nor negative. The greatest negative integer is -1, and the smallest positive integer is 1.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A bird is flying at an altitude of 100 meters above sea level. A fish is swimming at a depth of 50 meters below sea level. What is the vertical distance between the bird and the fish?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The bird is at +100 m and the fish is at -50 m. The vertical distance is the difference between their positions: 100 - (-50) = 100 + 50 = 150 meters.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the result of 5 - (-2)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Subtracting a negative number is equivalent to adding its positive counterpart. So, 5 - (-2) = 5 + 2 = 7.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which number is the additive inverse of 7?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The additive inverse of a number is the number that, when added to the original number, results in zero. For 7, the additive inverse is -7, because 7 + (-7) = 0.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Starting from -4, if you move 6 units to the right on a number line, and then 3 units to the left, what integer do you reach?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting at -4, moving 6 units to the right means adding 6: -4 + 6 = 2. Then, moving 3 units to the left means subtracting 3: 2 - 3 = -1.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Compare -10 and -1. Which of the following is correct?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On a number line, numbers increase as you move to the right. Since -1 is to the right of -10, -1 is greater than -10, meaning -10 is less than -1.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If the current temperature is -3°C and it drops by 5°C, what will be the new temperature?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: A drop in temperature means subtraction. So, the new temperature will be -3°C - 5°C = -8°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: In mathematics, what does the term "The Other Side of Zero" primarily refer to?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: "The Other Side of Zero" refers to the numbers located to the left of zero on the number line, which are negative numbers.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which integer correctly represents a temperature of 15 degrees Celsius below zero?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Below zero indicates a negative value, so 15 degrees Celsius below zero is represented as -15°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A diver is 25 meters below sea level. How would you represent his position using an integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Positions below sea level are considered negative values, so 25 meters below sea level is represented as -25.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: On a number line, where are negative integers located relative to zero?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: By convention, negative integers are placed to the left of zero on a horizontal number line.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following represents a loss of ₹750 in a business transaction?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: A loss is represented by a negative integer, so a loss of ₹750 is represented as -₹750.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following integers is the smallest?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On a number line, the further a number is to the left, the smaller its value. Therefore, -10 is the smallest.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Compare the following integers: -8 ____ -2. Which symbol makes the statement true?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On the number line, -8 is to the left of -2, which means -8 is smaller than -2. So, -8 < -2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Arrange the following integers in ascending order: -7, 3, 0, -4, 1.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Ascending order means from smallest to largest. On the number line, -7 is the smallest, followed by -4, then 0, 1, and finally 3.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the opposite of the integer -12?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The opposite of an integer is the number that is the same distance from zero on the number line but in the opposite direction. The opposite of -12 is 12.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the result of adding -9 and 4?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: When adding integers with different signs, subtract their absolute values and keep the sign of the number with the larger absolute value. | -9 | - | 4 | = 9 - 4 = 5. Since 9 is larger and negative, the answer is -5.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Find the sum: (-6) + (-10).
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: When adding integers with the same sign, add their absolute values and keep the common sign. So, 6 + 10 = 16, and since both are negative, the sum is -16.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Subtract 5 from -3.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Subtracting 5 from -3 means -3 - 5. This is equivalent to adding a negative number: -3 + (-5), which equals -8.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Calculate the value of: 8 - (-4).
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive counterpart. So, 8 - (-4) becomes 8 + 4, which equals 12.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A submarine is at 100 meters below sea level. It then rises 30 meters. What is its new position?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Initial position is -100m. Rising 30m means adding 30. So, -100 + 30 = -70m, which is 70 meters below sea level.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If your bank account has a balance of ₹800 and you withdraw ₹1200, what will be your new balance?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting balance is ₹800. Withdrawing ₹1200 means 800 - 1200. This calculation results in -₹400, indicating an overdraft or debt.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following integers is neither positive nor negative?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Zero (0) is a unique integer that is neither positive nor negative; it is the point of origin on the number line.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: How many integers are there between -5 and 2 (excluding -5 and 2)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The integers between -5 and 2 are -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1. Counting these gives 6 integers.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: On a number line, if you start at -2 and move 6 steps to the right, what integer do you land on?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting at -2 and moving 6 steps to the right means adding 6. So, -2 + 6 = 4.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: The temperature in Shimla was -5°C on Monday. On Tuesday, it dropped by 3°C. What was the temperature on Tuesday?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Dropping by 3°C means subtracting 3. So, -5°C - 3°C = -8°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: The elevation of a town is 150 meters below sea level. Another town is 80 meters higher than the first town. What is the elevation of the second town?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The first town's elevation is -150m. Being 80m higher means -150 + 80 = -70m.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following operations will result in a negative integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Let's calculate each: 5 + (-3) = 2; (-2) + (-4) = -6; 7 - 2 = 5; (-8) - (-10) = -8 + 10 = 2. Only (-2) + (-4) results in a negative integer.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the integer that comes immediately before -10 on the number line?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Moving one step to the left on the number line gives the number immediately before. So, -10 - 1 = -11.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the integer that comes immediately after -6 on the number line?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Moving one step to the right on the number line gives the number immediately after. So, -6 + 1 = -5.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If a withdrawal of ₹500 is represented by -500, how would a deposit of ₹700 be represented?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: A deposit is the opposite of a withdrawal. If withdrawal is negative, a deposit is positive, so it's represented as 700.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the result of adding an integer and its opposite?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: An integer and its opposite (additive inverse) always sum up to zero. For example, 5 + (-5) = 0.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A bird is flying at 20 meters above the ground, and a fish is swimming at 5 meters below sea level. What is the difference in their vertical positions?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The bird's position is +20m. The fish's position is -5m. The difference is calculated as 20 - (-5) = 20 + 5 = 25 meters.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following statements about integers is FALSE?
options: All negative integers are smaller than zero.
All positive integers are greater than zero.
Zero is the smallest positive integer.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Zero is neither positive nor negative. The smallest positive integer is 1.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If point P represents -3 on a number line, and point Q is 5 units to the right of P, what integer does Q represent?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting at -3 and moving 5 units to the right means adding 5. So, -3 + 5 = 2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: The temperature rose from -10°C to 2°C. By how many degrees did the temperature rise?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: To find the rise in temperature, subtract the initial temperature from the final temperature: 2°C - (-10°C) = 2°C + 10°C = 12°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following represents '100 meters below sea level'?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Below sea level is represented by a negative integer, so 100 meters below sea level is -100 m.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the integer that represents 'a loss of ₹500'?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: A loss is represented by a negative integer, so a loss of ₹500 is -₹500.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: On a number line, which number is to the left of -3?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On a number line, numbers to the left are smaller. -4 is smaller than -3 and thus to its left.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the additive inverse of -9?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The additive inverse of a number is the number that, when added to the original number, results in zero. The additive inverse of -9 is 9 because -9 + 9 = 0.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Compare: -5 ____ 2
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Any negative number is smaller than any positive number. So, -5 is less than 2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the result of 5 + (-3)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting its absolute value. So, 5 + (-3) = 5 - 3 = 2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following integers is the greatest?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Zero is greater than any negative integer. Among the given options, 0 is the greatest.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If you move 4 steps to the right from 0 on a number line, what integer do you reach?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Moving to the right on a number line represents increasing values or positive numbers. 4 steps to the right from 0 reaches 4.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the value of (-7) + 7?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: When a number is added to its additive inverse, the result is always zero.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: The temperature in Shimla was -4°C on Monday. It rose by 6°C on Tuesday. What was the temperature on Tuesday?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting at -4°C and rising by 6°C means -4 + 6 = 2°C.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Arrange the following integers in ascending order: -8, 5, 0, -3, 2.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Ascending order means from smallest to largest. Negative numbers are smaller than positive numbers. The order is -8, -3, 0, 2, 5.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A submarine is at a depth of 250 meters below sea level. It ascends 100 meters. What is its new depth?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Below sea level is negative, so initial depth is -250 m. Ascending means adding, so -250 + 100 = -150 m.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the value of 12 - (-5)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive counterpart. So, 12 - (-5) = 12 + 5 = 17.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What integer should be added to -15 to get 10?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Let the integer be x. Then -15 + x = 10. To find x, add 15 to both sides: x = 10 + 15 = 25.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which statement is true about integers on a number line?
options: Every positive integer is to the left of 0.
Every negative integer is to the right of 0.
All negative integers are smaller than all positive integers.
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: On a number line, numbers increase from left to right. All negative integers are smaller than all positive integers.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Find the sum of -8, 5, and -2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: An elevator is on the 3rd floor. It goes down 5 floors. On which floor is it now?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Starting at 3rd floor and going down 5 floors means 3 - 5 = -2. This indicates 2 floors below ground level.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the value of (-3) + (-4)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: When adding two negative numbers, add their absolute values and keep the negative sign. So, (-3) + (-4) = -(3+4) = -7.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: How many integers are there between -3 and 4 (excluding -3 and 4)?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The integers between -3 and 4 are -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. Counting them gives 6 integers.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: An integer is 5 units to the right of -7 on the number line. What is this integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Moving to the right on a number line means adding. So, -7 + 5 = -2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the integer that is 4 units to the left of 0, and then 6 units to the right from that position?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: 4 units to the left of 0 is -4. From -4, moving 6 units to the right means -4 + 6 = 2.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A person gains ₹2500, then loses ₹1200, and finally gains another ₹800. What is the net financial change?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Gain is positive, loss is negative. So, 2500 - 1200 + 800 = 1300 + 800 = 2100. This is a gain of ₹2100.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If the sum of two integers is -15 and one of them is 7, what is the other integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Let the other integer be x. Then 7 + x = -15. To find x, subtract 7 from both sides: x = -15 - 7 = -22.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: Which of the following expressions has the smallest value?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: Let's evaluate each expression: A) -5 + 2 = -3; B) 5 - (-2) = 5 + 2 = 7; C) -5 - 2 = -7; D) 2 - 5 = -3. The smallest value is -7.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: What is the difference between the smallest two-digit negative integer and the smallest two-digit positive integer?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The smallest two-digit negative integer is -99. The smallest two-digit positive integer is 10. The difference is -99 - 10 = -109.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: If 'A' represents an integer such that A > -3 and A < 2, how many possible integer values can 'A' take?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The integers greater than -3 are -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ... The integers less than 2 are ..., -1, 0, 1. Combining these conditions, A can be -2, -1, 0, 1. There are 4 such values.

6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.subject: Mathematics
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.question: A diver is 15 meters below sea level. A bird is flying 8 meters above sea level. What is the vertical distance between the diver and the bird?
6::Mathematics::the-other-side-of-zero.explanation: The diver's position is -15 meters. The bird's position is +8 meters. The vertical distance between them is the difference between the higher position and the lower position: 8 - (-15) = 8 + 15 = 23 meters.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the main purpose of science?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science primarily aims to explore, observe, and understand how the natural world works through systematic investigation and experimentation.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is a branch of science that specifically studies living organisms?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Biology is the scientific study of life, focusing on living organisms, their structure, function, growth, origin, evolution, and distribution.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What tool would a scientist use to observe very tiny objects like cells or bacteria?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A microscope is an optical instrument designed to magnify small objects, making it possible to see things invisible to the naked eye.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Who is widely known for discovering the law of universal gravitation after observing a falling apple?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation, a fundamental law describing the gravitational attraction between all objects with mass.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which step typically comes first in a scientific investigation?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: The scientific method usually begins with making an observation about something intriguing or unexplained, which then leads to questions.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is a 'hypothesis' in the context of science?
options: An educated guess that can be tested
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation for a phenomenon, which is based on prior observations and can be tested through experimentation.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is it important for scientific experiments to be repeatable by other scientists?
options: To ensure the results are reliable and not just a fluke
To find new uses for the equipment
To prove the first scientist was wrong
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Repeatability ensures that the experimental results are consistent and reliable across different conditions and researchers, validating the findings.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of how science benefits our daily life?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: While science can inspire fictional stories, its direct benefit lies in practical applications like health, technology, and understanding natural phenomena, not in creating fiction itself.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the name of the scientific instrument used to view distant objects like stars and planets?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A telescope is an optical instrument used to observe distant objects by collecting and focusing electromagnetic radiation.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the main difference between a scientific theory and a scientific law?
options: A law is a guess, a theory is proven.
A theory explains 'why' something happens, a law describes 'what' happens.
A law is always wrong, a theory is always right.
There is no difference, they are the same.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A scientific law describes an observed phenomenon, often mathematically, while a scientific theory provides a well-substantiated explanation for that phenomenon.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Dr. C.V. Raman, an Indian physicist, won the Nobel Prize for his work on the scattering of light. What is this phenomenon famously known as?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Dr. C.V. Raman discovered that when light passes through a transparent material, some of the deflected light changes wavelength, a phenomenon called the Raman Effect.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What kind of thinking encourages asking questions, seeking evidence, and avoiding superstitions?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Scientific thinking emphasizes critical analysis, logical reasoning, and relying on empirical evidence rather than unsubstantiated beliefs or superstitions.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: If an experiment yields results that contradict the initial hypothesis, what should a scientist typically do?
options: Ignore the results and declare the hypothesis correct
Change the results to match the hypothesis
Re-evaluate the hypothesis and conduct more experiments or modify the existing ones
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Contradictory results are crucial in science; they prompt scientists to revise their hypothesis, design new experiments, or re-examine their methods to understand the discrepancies.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of the following best describes the process of 'inference' in science?
options: Making a prediction about the future
Forming a conclusion based on observations and prior knowledge
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: An inference is a logical conclusion or interpretation drawn from observations and existing knowledge, rather than a direct observation itself.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these qualities is most crucial for a scientist when exploring new ideas or phenomena?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Curiosity drives the desire to explore and understand the unknown, while an open mind allows scientists to consider new possibilities and adapt to evidence.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the primary goal of science?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science aims to systematically observe, experiment, and explain the phenomena of the natural and physical world.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which branch of science deals with the study of living organisms?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Biology is the natural science that studies life and living organisms, including their structure, function, growth, evolution, distribution, and taxonomy.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the first step in the scientific method?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: The scientific method begins with observing a phenomenon or asking a question about the natural world.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is a tool used by scientists to see very tiny objects?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A microscope is an optical instrument used to observe objects that are too small to be seen normally with the naked eye.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the main characteristic that distinguishes living things from non-living things?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Living things exhibit growth, reproduction, response to stimuli, and cellular organization, which non-living things generally do not.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which Indian scientist is famous for his work on the structure of DNA?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Har Gobind Khorana was an Indian-American biochemist who shared the Nobel Prize for his work on the interpretation of the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: A testable prediction about the outcome of an experiment is called a:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation for a phenomenon, which is testable through experimentation.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the study of matter and energy, and how they interact?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Physics is the branch of science concerned with the nature and properties of matter and energy. It covers mechanics, heat, light and other radiation, sound, electricity, magnetism, and the structure of atoms.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is it important for scientists to share their findings?
options: To allow others to verify results
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sharing findings allows other scientists to reproduce experiments, verify results, build upon existing knowledge, and ensure the reliability of scientific discoveries.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of the following is an example of an observation?
options: The sky is blue because of reflection.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: An observation is gathering information through our senses; 'the leaf turned yellow' is a direct sensory input. The others are inferences or predictions.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the controlled variable in an experiment?
options: The variable that is changed by the scientist.
The variables that are kept the same.
The final result of the experiment.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Controlled variables (or constants) are elements in an experiment that are kept unchanged to ensure that only the independent variable affects the dependent variable.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: If you want to study the composition and properties of different substances, which branch of science would you focus on?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Chemistry is the scientific discipline involved with elements and compounds composed of atoms, molecules, and ions: their composition, structure, properties, behavior, and the changes they undergo during a reaction with other substances.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Space Program'?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is widely regarded as the Father of the Indian Space Program for his crucial role in establishing the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the purpose of forming a conclusion in the scientific method?
options: To state whether the hypothesis was supported or rejected
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A conclusion states whether the data from an experiment supported or did not support the initial hypothesis, based on the analysis of the results.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is a characteristic of all living things?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: All known living organisms are composed of one or more cells, which are the basic structural and functional units of life.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is it important to have a 'control group' in an experiment?
options: To ensure all variables are changed
To compare results against a baseline
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A control group serves as a baseline for comparison, allowing scientists to see the effect of the independent variable by comparing it to a group where the variable is not applied.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What kind of energy do plants primarily use for photosynthesis?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Plants use light energy, typically from the sun, to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (food) and oxygen in the process of photosynthesis.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What does a seismograph measure?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A seismograph is an instrument that detects and records ground motion during an earthquake, measuring its intensity and duration.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of the following is an example of applying scientific knowledge in daily life?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Cooking food involves understanding heat transfer, chemical reactions, and physical changes, all based on scientific principles.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: When an object moves from one place to another, what is it undergoing?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Motion is the change in position of an object over time, which is a fundamental concept in physics.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which Indian scientist won the Nobel Prize for his work on the scattering of light (Raman Effect)?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sir C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his discovery of the 'Raman Effect,' which explains the change in the wavelength of light that occurs when a light beam is deflected by molecules.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What happens if an experiment yields results that contradict the hypothesis?
options: The experiment is discarded as a failure.
The hypothesis must be revised or rejected.
The data must be changed to fit the hypothesis.
The scientist must repeat the experiment until it works.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: If experimental results do not support the hypothesis, it means the initial explanation might be incorrect and requires revision or rejection to form a new hypothesis.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A thermometer is a device used for measuring temperature or a temperature gradient, typically using a mercury or alcohol column or an electronic sensor.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is a 'theory' in science?
options: An idea that cannot be tested
A well-substantiated explanation of some aspect of the natural world, based on a body of facts
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: In science, a theory is a comprehensive explanation supported by a vast body of evidence, repeatedly tested and confirmed through observation and experimentation, much more robust than a simple guess.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The study of the Earth's physical structure, substance, history, and the processes that act on it is called:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Geology is the science that deals with the Earth's physical structure and substance, its history, and the processes that act on it.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why do scientists often work in teams?
options: To make decisions faster without discussion
To share knowledge and different expertise
To avoid doing all the work themselves
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Teamwork in science allows researchers to combine diverse knowledge, skills, and perspectives, leading to more comprehensive and innovative solutions to complex problems.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the phenomenon where a liquid turns into a gas, like water boiling?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Evaporation is the process by which a substance in a liquid state changes to a gaseous state due to an increase in temperature or pressure.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a scientific experiment?
options: It must have a testable hypothesis.
It should only prove what the scientist wants to believe.
It should aim to collect objective data.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A scientific experiment should be designed to objectively test a hypothesis, not to merely confirm preconceived notions. The goal is to discover truth, regardless of expectation.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the process called where living organisms make more of their own kind?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Reproduction is a fundamental biological process by which new individual organisms – 'offspring' – are produced from their 'parents'.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: If you observe that a plant watered with saltwater dies, and a plant watered with fresh water thrives, what would be a reasonable inference?
options: Saltwater might be harmful to plants.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: An inference is a conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning. Based on the observation, it is reasonable to infer that saltwater is detrimental to the plant's health.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is generally considered the first step in the scientific method?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: The scientific method often begins with making careful observations about a phenomenon and then asking questions based on what is observed.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The branch of science that focuses on studying living organisms, including plants and animals, is called:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Biology is the natural science that studies life and living organisms, covering their structure, function, growth, evolution, and classification.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which scientific instrument helps us see very tiny objects that are invisible to the naked eye, such as bacteria?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A microscope is an optical instrument used to magnify small objects, allowing us to observe details that are otherwise too tiny to be seen.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: A scientist always tries to find answers and explanations based on:
options: Evidence gathered through observation and experiments
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science relies on empirical evidence obtained through systematic observation and rigorous experimentation, rather than subjective opinions or beliefs.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is an example of how science has helped improve communication in daily life?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Mobile phones are a direct result of scientific advancements in electronics and telecommunications, enabling instant communication across vast distances.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: After making observations, a scientist often proposes a testable explanation or an educated guess. What is this called?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for an observation, made on the basis of limited evidence, which can then be tested through experiments.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Who was the Indian physicist known for his groundbreaking work on light scattering, which led to the discovery of the 'Raman Effect' and a Nobel Prize in Physics?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sir C.V. Raman was an eminent Indian physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his discovery that when light traverses a transparent material, some of the deflected light changes wavelength and amplitude.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: An instrument primarily used to observe distant celestial objects like stars and planets is a:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: A telescope is an optical instrument designed to make distant objects, such as stars and planets, appear magnified and closer.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is it important for scientists to repeat their experiments multiple times?
options: To make the experiment last longer
To obtain different results each time
To ensure the results are reliable and consistent
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Repeating experiments, or replication, helps to confirm that the initial results were not due to chance or error, thereby increasing the reliability and validity of the findings.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Science helps us understand the world around us by consistently asking which types of questions?
options: "Who is the best?" and "What is fair?"
"How much money?" and "When is it due?"
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science is driven by curiosity, constantly asking 'why' things happen and exploring 'what if' scenarios to understand natural phenomena.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The famous scientist known for formulating the laws of motion and the universal law of gravitation is:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton was a pivotal figure in the scientific revolution, whose work laid the foundation for classical mechanics through his laws of motion and gravity.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which quality is most essential for a scientist to successfully discover new things?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Curiosity drives scientists to ask questions, and keen observation skills allow them to gather the information needed to explore those questions, both fundamental to scientific inquiry.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What should you always do before touching any unknown substance in a science lab or experiment?
options: Smell it directly by putting your nose close
Ask your teacher or a responsible adult for instructions
Touch it with your bare hands quickly
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Safety is paramount in science. You should never handle unknown substances without proper guidance from a teacher or an adult to prevent potential harm or accidents.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: How has science significantly improved modern transportation compared to ancient methods?
options: By making vehicles heavier and slower
By enabling much faster and safer travel over long distances
By reducing the need for roads and pathways
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Scientific advancements in fields like engineering, aerodynamics, and materials science have led to the creation of vehicles that allow for significantly faster, safer, and more efficient travel across the globe.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The idea that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction is a fundamental principle in which branch of science?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: This statement is Newton's Third Law of Motion, a foundational concept in Physics that describes the interaction between forces.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of these is NOT a tool commonly used for making measurements in science?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Rulers measure length, measuring cylinders measure volume, and balances measure mass; a storybook is not a scientific measurement tool.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: When you use your senses to notice that a plant's leaves are turning yellow, you are making an:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: An observation involves directly gathering information using your senses, such as seeing the change in leaf color.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, often leading to the creation of useful tools and machines, is known as:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Technology refers to the application of scientific knowledge for practical objectives, such as inventing new devices or methods to solve problems.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Science plays a crucial role in finding solutions for major global problems like:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Medical science and public health research are dedicated to understanding diseases, developing treatments, and improving overall human health and well-being.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The branch of science that studies the composition, structure, properties, and reactions of matter is called:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Chemistry is the scientific study of substances, including their elements, compounds, properties, and how they interact and change during chemical reactions.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: The principle behind how an electric bulb glows when switched on primarily involves the conversion of electrical energy into which other forms of energy?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: When electricity passes through the filament of an incandescent bulb, it heats up due to resistance, causing it to emit both light (light energy) and significant heat (heat energy).

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which of the following statements about the nature of science is TRUE?
options: Science never changes, its ideas are fixed forever.
Scientific ideas are always proven absolutely correct and cannot be challenged.
Science involves continuously questioning ideas and testing them with evidence.
Science relies on magic and supernatural explanations.
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science is a dynamic process of inquiry where existing ideas are constantly re-evaluated, questioned, and refined based on new evidence and discoveries.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: In a scientific experiment, the facts and information collected are referred to as:
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Data refers to the observations, measurements, and other facts systematically collected during an experiment, which are then analyzed to draw conclusions.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Which branch of science is primarily concerned with studying the Earth, its physical structure, composition, history, and the processes shaping it?
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Geology is the natural science that studies the Earth, including its composition, physical characteristics, processes, and history, along with the study of rocks, minerals, and landforms.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What does it mean for a scientist to be 'skeptical'?
options: To believe everything they hear without questioning
To refuse to believe anything at all
To question claims and demand evidence before accepting them
To only believe what their friends tell them
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Scientific skepticism means critically examining claims and arguments, demanding evidence, and being open to revising beliefs when new evidence is presented.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is scientific progress often described as a 'cumulative process'?
options: Because scientists tend to forget older discoveries
Because new scientific discoveries usually contradict and completely replace older ones
Because new knowledge and discoveries are built upon and extend existing scientific understanding
Because scientists prefer to work on completely new problems rather than old ones
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Science is cumulative because each new discovery and understanding builds upon previous knowledge, leading to a deeper and more comprehensive understanding of the natural world over time.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: What is the main purpose of conducting an experiment in science?
options: To simply make a guess about something
To prove that the scientist is always right
To systematically test a hypothesis or answer a specific question
To entertain and impress other people
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: An experiment is a controlled procedure designed to test a hypothesis, gather data, and determine the cause-and-effect relationships between variables.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: Why is it important for scientists to openly share their findings and research methods with the global scientific community?
options: To keep their discoveries secret from the public
To confuse other scientists with complex information
To allow other scientists to verify results, reproduce experiments, and build upon the work
To ensure that only a few people know about new advancements
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.explanation: Sharing findings is crucial for peer review, replication of experiments to confirm reliability, and to enable the broader scientific community to expand upon existing knowledge, accelerating progress.

6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.subject: Science
6::Science::the-wonderful-world-of-scien.question: A scientist observes that plants watered with a specific type of solution grow taller. To confirm this result, what is the *most crucial* element for a controlled experiment?
options: Watering all plants with the same solution
Not watering any plants at all
Comparing plants watered with the solution to identical plants watered with plain water
Giving different amounts of solution to each plant without a comparison group
